I expect those offsets to keep the March decline under 5%, then weaken enough for coal and surcharge losses to push the April–June decline to at least 5%.

I expect the acquisition contribution to help keep March above -5%, with pressure across those businesses taking reported April–June revenue growth to -5% or lower.

A further slowdown of about 3.25 percentage points per quarter would leave March near -2.6% and put June near -5.9% if pricing offsets less of the volume loss.

December product sales still fell 2.1% on lower volume, and customers were resisting higher prices (A, B, D). Renewed volume losses could deepen the consolidated decline to at least 5% in June.

Kennametal's net sales held near $482 million in both quarters, but the year-over-year shortfall widened from $10.5 million to $13.3 million, taking growth from -2.14% to -2.68%. That pace favors March staying above -5%. A June crossing would require the decline to accelerate, making this a lower-confidence alert.

Astec's December net sales grew 6.47%, supporting a March result above -5%. Yet it entered 2025 with $150.2 million fewer orders in backlog than a year earlier, a 26.4% drop (B, C). As it ships those orders, the smaller backlog raises the risk of a June sales decline of at least 5% unless new orders fill the gap.

ACI's quarterly revenue was nearly unchanged sequentially at about $452 million to $453 million, yet year-over-year growth swung from +24.44% to -4.9364%. Full-year growth of 10% (A) supports March staying above -5%, but the quarterly swings and December's 0.064-point cushion make a June crossing plausible. Timing is uncertain.

Union Pacific's total revenue growth slowed from +2.52% in September to -0.62% in December. Lower fuel surcharges and a shift toward lower-revenue intermodal shipments limited annual freight revenue growth to 1% despite 3% volume growth and pricing gains (A, B). If the quarterly slowdown continues at roughly 3.1 points per quarter, March would be near -3.8% and June near -6.9%.

CSX's total revenue growth fell from +1.32% in September to -3.83% in December. Merchandise pricing gains and higher volumes could keep March above -5% (B). Lower fuel recovery, coal rates and trucking surcharges (A, C) could push June through the threshold if those offsets weaken.

J.B. Hunt's quarterly revenue declines widened from 3.02% to 4.76%, with both quarters still above the cutoff. Lower volumes across three segments and lower revenue per load across two (B) support a June decline of at least 5%. The timing is close: March must stay above -5%, and December had only 0.24 percentage points of room.
